scenarios.title: Epoxide safety alert
scenarios.story: A toxicology team is triaging compounds before synthesis. Epoxides are reactive and can damage DNA, so every one has to be counted and flagged.
scenarios.question: Epoxides are reactive and can damage DNA, so they are flagged in safety screens. Count the epoxide rings (C1OC1) in this molecule. Provide a whole number. Give your answer as an integer.
scenarios.displayQuestion: This drug candidate looks promising, but first I need to check it for DNA-damaging epoxide groups. How many does it have?
scenarios.payoff: Post-trained Nemotron found all {expected}. Base Nemotron didn’t, so a toxic candidate could have slipped through.
scenarios.speaker: Toxicologist
scenarios.intro: A toxicologist is researching drug safety…

glossary.definition: A tiny ring of two carbon atoms and one oxygen atom. The ring is strained, so it reacts easily, including with DNA, which is why it can be toxic.

scenarios.title: Oral absorption (Lipinski)
scenarios.story: A project team is deciding whether a compound is likely to be absorbed orally. Hydrogen-bond donor count is one of the Lipinski rule-of-five checks.
scenarios.question: Hydrogen-bond donors matter for oral absorption (Lipinski rule of five). What is the count of hydrogen bond donors in this molecule? Give your answer as an integer.
scenarios.speaker: Medicinal chemist
scenarios.intro: A medicinal chemist is designing an oral drug…
scenarios.displayQuestion: This compound looks promising, but a pill has to be absorbed through the gut, and too many hydrogen-bond donors can block that. How many does it have?
scenarios.payoff: Post-trained Nemotron counted all {expected}. Base Nemotron didn’t, so the chemist could misjudge whether the drug can be absorbed.

glossary.definition: Hydrogen atoms attached to nitrogen or oxygen (as in –NH₂ or –OH) that can bond to other molecules. Too many make it harder for a drug to cross cell membranes.

scenarios.title: Alkylating agent alert
scenarios.story: A safety scientist is checking a candidate for alkylating groups, which can react with DNA and cause genotoxicity.
scenarios.question: Alkyl halides can act as alkylating, potentially genotoxic agents. How many total alkyl halides in the following compound? Give your answer as an integer.

scenarios.title: Aromatic amine alert
scenarios.story: A medicinal chemist is reviewing a lead series. Aromatic amines (anilines) are a well-known toxicity alert, so each one needs to be found.
scenarios.question: Aromatic amines (anilines) are a well-known toxicity alert. Determine the number of anilines (Ar-NH2) in the molecule below. Give your answer as an integer. Give your answer as an integer.

scenarios.title: Lactone stability
scenarios.story: A formulation team is assessing stability. Lactones can ring-open in the body and change how a drug behaves.
scenarios.question: Lactones can ring-open in the body and change a drug's activity. Identify the number of cyclic esters (lactones) in the following compound. Give your answer as an integer.
